note:
Regenerated 2026-10-28 at git_sha 0758fa0 (change perf-baseline-refresh-2026-10).

WHY (this is NOT a code regression): four independent pieces of evidence, all measured.

(1) DEPENDENCY CLOSURE — the perf binaries contain none of the code that changed
    since the previous baseline was captured:
      - `perf_tests`' compile closure
        (build/tests/benchmark/CMakeFiles/perf_tests.dir/perf_main.cpp.o.d)
        contains ZERO headers under include/cpu/** (measured 2026-10-28);
      - the whole `cpphdl` library's closure likewise
        (`grep -rl 'include/cpu/' build/CMakeFiles/cpphdl.dir/` => no hit).
    => every RV32I / cache change of 2026-10-25..28 (rv32i-store-byte-enable,
       rv32i-forwarding-decision, rv32i-fetch-skid-buffer, rv32i-jump-sra,
       rv32i-load-byte-lane, riscv-mini-cache-wrapper-live-logic) is NOT in the
       perf binary.

(2) THE ONLY TWO perf-closure FILES THAT CHANGED (git diff 7c5038e..HEAD) are
    `src/jit/jit_compiler.cpp` and `src/simulator.cpp`, and BOTH changes are pure
    ERROR-PATH ATTRIBUTION (commit 618262d):
      - jit_compiler.cpp: sets `last_error_msg_` on the two FAILURE exits
        (>64-bit node in allocate_buffer; unsupported node type in generate_ir)
        => runs ONLY when JIT compilation FAILS; the hot path is untouched;
      - simulator.cpp: rewrites the CHINFO format string inside the JIT-fallback
        branch of try_jit_compile() => executed only on that same failure path.
    => ZERO hot-path (interpreter / JIT codegen / execute) change
    => a real regression would have to come from these two files; they cannot
       produce one.

(3) HOST STATE — the collection ran on an IDLE host:
      - 4 cores / 15.7 GB RAM; load average at the start of the first sample
        1.52 / 1.77 / 2.19 (the 1-min figure is the tail of the previous
        session's own work, not a concurrent build);
      - NO concurrent `ctest` / `cmake --build` / `cc1plus` process was running
        (`ps` check before the window; the only load during the window was the
        perf run itself);
      - cgroup: `cpu.cfs_quota_us = -1` (UNLIMITED), `cpu.stat` reports
        `nr_throttled = 0` => no CPU throttling;
      - /proc/stat sampling during the window: `steal = 0.00%` => no
        hypervisor steal.

(4) THE CODE UNDER MEASUREMENT WAS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS ALL SAMPLES
    (no commit touched the perf closure between them) => every difference
    between samples is measurement noise, by construction. The measured
    run-to-run spread is reported per row below.

SAMPLING PROCEDURE (why 3 runs and a per-row median):
  The previous baseline was produced by a SINGLE `perf_tests --all` run, and the
  run-to-run spread of this host is NOT negligible: several rows are BIMODAL
  (e.g. TC-11 regs=10 lands at ~54 ms in one run and at ~94-103 ms in another
  => a 1.87x gap between two modes of the SAME binary). A single sample
  therefore risks recording either an over-estimate (=> the gate silently
  loosens) or an under-estimate (=> the gate reports false regressions).
  => 3 independent runs of the SAME ctest entry (identical flags as CI:
     `perf_tests --all --verilator=<wrapper> --report=json --report=csv
     --report=md`, wall-clock 908.90 s / 899.87 s / 863.20 s) on an idle host,
     and the baseline records the PER-ROW MEDIAN of the 3 samples.
  => The median (not the min, not the max) is used precisely so that NO sample
     is cherry-picked in either direction; all per-sample values are listed
     below so a reviewer can recompute the median.
  => The median lands on the row's MAJORITY MODE, which is what makes the gate
     robust against the bimodality: for TC-11 regs=10 jit the median is the
     slow mode (93.8 ms) => the fast mode (54.6 ms) yields ratio 0.58 (no
     regression) and the slow mode yields 1.09 (no regression) => NEITHER mode
     trips the gate. (Had the baseline been the fast mode, the slow mode would
     have been 1.87x => above the 1.6x threshold => a false regression.)

  ⚠️ A HYPOTHESIS THAT WAS MEASURED AND FALSIFIED (kept here because the
  obvious next step for a maintainer is to repeat it): a standalone
  `perf_tests --tc=11` run measured TC-11 regs=10 at ~54 ms, while the first two
  `--all` samples measured ~94-103 ms. The natural inference was "the
  collection command matters" (the `--all` path runs TC-01/02/04/06 in-process
  and spawns 9 TC-07/08/09 children before TC-11, so the parent process's prior
  state differs). The THIRD `--all` sample then measured the same row at
  53.5 ms => the standalone run had merely landed in the other mode; the
  command is NOT the discriminator. => the discriminator is the bimodality
  itself. => All baseline samples were nevertheless collected with the SAME
  command CI uses, so that no inference about path equivalence is needed.

  ⚠️ The row's other fields (build_us / sim_us / total_us / ticks_per_sec /
  ns_per_tick / iterations / status / skip_reason) are taken from the sample
  whose `median_us` IS the median => each row stays internally consistent
  (e.g. `sim_us` still matches `median_us`).

WALL-CLOCK: the 3 samples took 908.90 s / 899.87 s / 863.20 s on this host.
The CTest TIMEOUT for `perf_tests` is 1800 s, which satisfies the contract's
`1.5 x measured_wall_clock + 300` for the reference-workstation measurement
(930 s => 1695 s) and also for this host's measurement (~905 s => 1657 s).
